감사합니다.x: Thank you so much for the gift.
감사합니다.e: 감사 (thanks) + 합니다 (I do) — the formal 'thank you'.

형제.x: Do you have any brothers or sisters?

우체국.x: I sent a package at the post office.

목.x: I caught a cold, so my throat hurts.
목.t: 목이 아파요 can mean a sore throat or a stiff neck.

등산.x: My father goes hiking every weekend.
등산.e: Literally 'climbing a mountain' — a hugely popular weekend hobby in Korea.
등산.t: Both 등산을 하다 and 등산을 가다 (go hiking) are common.

깨끗하다.x: The hotel room is very clean.

충전하다.m: to charge (a battery); to top up, to reload (a card)
충전하다.x: I put 10,000 won on my transit card at the convenience store.
충전하다.e: Literally 'fill with electricity' + 하다; also used for adding money.
충전하다.t: Koreans also say they need to 충전 themselves, meaning recharge with rest.

양념.ex: 고기에 양념을 하고 한 시간 동안 두세요.
양념.x: Season the meat and leave it for an hour.
양념.e: Probably from older 약념, 'medicinal seasoning' — spices were thought to be good for health.
양념.t: Pronounced [양념]; at chicken shops, 양념 means the sweet-spicy red sauce vs. 후라이드 (fried).

어떻다.m: to be how, to be what like
어떻다.ex: 한국에 온 지 한 달 됐는데 생활은 어때요?
어떻다.x: It's been a month since you came to Korea — how's life here?
어떻다.e: Short for 어떠하다; the question member of the set 이렇다, 그렇다, 저렇다.
어떻다.t: N은/는 어때요? asks opinions or makes suggestions: 내일은 어때요? = How about tomorrow?

강조하다.x: The teacher stressed pronunciation several times.

공손하다.ex: 그 학생은 선생님께 항상 공손하게 인사해요.
공손하다.x: That student always greets the teacher politely.

흑자.x: Our company went back into the black for the first time in three years.
흑자.e: Literally 'black letters' — profits were written in black ink, just like 'in the black'.
흑자.t: Pronounced [흑짜]: the ㅈ after ㄱ becomes tense.

밝혀지다.m: to be revealed, to come to light, to be found out
밝혀지다.x: The investigation revealed the cause of the accident.
밝혀지다.e: 밝히다 'to make bright, to reveal' + -어지다 'become': brought into the light.
밝혀지다.t: Pronounced [발켜지다]: ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

문해력.ex: 최근 청소년들의 문해력이 떨어졌다는 기사가 많습니다.
문해력.x: There have been many articles recently saying teenagers' literacy has declined.
문해력.t: A popular news buzzword; it means understanding what you read, not just being able to read.

혁신.x: That company succeeded through constant innovation.
혁신.t: Pronounced [혁씬] — the ㅅ becomes tense after ㄱ.

정서.ex: 음악은 아이들의 정서 발달에 도움이 돼요.
정서.t: More formal than 감정; often means a shared sensibility, e.g. 한국인의 정서 'the Korean sensibility'.

버스킹.x: I saw a singer busking in front of Hongdae.
버스킹.t: 버스킹하다 = to busk; the performer is a 버스커. Buskers often need a permit for popular spots.

(이)라든지.forms: 이라든지 after a consonant (빵이라든지) · 라든지 after a vowel (과자라든지) · A(이)라든지 B(이)라든지
(이)라든지.ex: 과일이라든지 채소라든지 몸에 좋은 걸 드세요.
(이)라든지.x: Eat things that are good for you, like fruit or vegetables.
(이)라든지.e: From 이다 'to be' + -라든지, a quoting form of -든지: 'whether it's X or …'.
(이)라든지.t: Lists a few examples without being complete. In casual speech 같은 거 is similar: 과일 같은 거.

생리대.x: You can buy sanitary pads at convenience stores too.
생리대.t: Pronounced [생니대]. Sold at convenience stores, supermarkets and drugstores. A tampon is 탐폰.

핵폐기물.ex: 핵폐기물을 안전하게 보관하는 것은 어려운 문제입니다.
핵폐기물.x: Storing nuclear waste safely is a difficult problem.

당면하다.m: to face (a current problem), to be confronted with
당면하다.ex: 우리가 당면한 가장 큰 과제는 인구 감소입니다.
당면하다.x: The biggest task we face is population decline.
당면하다.e: Literally 'meeting it face to face' — right here, right now.

앞당기다.m: to move up, to bring forward (a date); to hasten
앞당기다.ex: 회의 날짜를 다음 주 월요일로 앞당겼어요.
앞당기다.x: We moved the meeting up to next Monday.
앞당기다.e: Built from 앞 'front' plus 당기다 'to pull' — pulling a date forward.

향유하다.ex: 모든 시민은 문화생활을 향유할 권리가 있습니다.
향유하다.x: All citizens have the right to enjoy cultural life.
향유하다.t: Formal; in conversation 누리다 is more natural.

코웃음을 치다.forms: 코웃음을 쳐요 · 코웃음을 쳤어요 · 코웃음을 칠 거예요
코웃음을 치다.ex: 제 계획을 듣고 친구는 코웃음을 쳤어요.
코웃음을 치다.x: My friend scoffed when he heard my plan.
코웃음을 치다.e: 코웃음 = a 'nose laugh': 코 'nose' + 웃음 'laugh,' a scornful snort.

명예 훼손.ex: 그 배우는 악성 댓글을 단 사람들을 명예 훼손으로 고소했습니다.
명예 훼손.x: The actor sued the people who posted malicious comments for defamation.

밀접 접촉자.x: I was classified as a close contact, so I got tested.
밀접 접촉자.t: Pronounced [밀쩝 접촉짜]. Health authorities use it: 밀접 접촉자로 분류되다 'to be classified as a close contact'.

공시지가.x: Seoul's officially assessed land prices rose sharply this year.
공시지가.t: Property taxes are based on 공시지가, which is usually lower than the market price, 시가.

송구하다.m: to be sorry, feel deeply apologetic (very formal)
송구하다.x: We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience.
송구하다.e: Literally 'fearful and afraid' — humbly frightened at having troubled someone.
송구하다.t: Very formal apology, used to superiors or in public statements; 송구합니다 is stronger than 죄송합니다.

재현성.ex: 과학 실험은 재현성이 있어야 믿을 수 있어요.
재현성.x: A scientific experiment must be reproducible to be trusted.

직유.x: 'Eyes as clear as a lake' is an expression that uses a simile.
직유.t: Spot it by 처럼, 같이 or 듯이; without those markers, it's usually 은유 (metaphor).

육이오.ex: 우리 할아버지는 육이오 때 부산으로 피란을 가셨어요.
육이오.x: My grandfather fled to Busan as a refugee during the Korean War.
육이오.e: Named after its start date, June 25, 1950; usually written 6·25.
육이오.t: Pronounced [유기오] — the ㄱ batchim links to the next syllable.

은연중.x: He revealed his true feelings without realizing it.
은연중.e: Literally 'in the midst of hiddenness': something that shows without anyone noticing.
은연중.t: Usually followed by 에: 은연중에 드러나다 means 'to show through unintentionally'.

동인.ex: 기술 발전은 사회 변화의 중요한 동인입니다.
동인.x: Technological progress is an important driving force of social change.
동인.t: Don't confuse with the homonym 동인 'fellow members', as in 동인지 'coterie magazine'.

수불석권.m: always reading, never putting a book down
수불석권.x: My grandfather never put down his books his whole life.
수불석권.e: Literally 'the hand never releases the scroll'.

고혈당.ex: 고혈당이 오래 계속되면 합병증이 생길 수 있어요.
고혈당.x: If high blood sugar continues for a long time, complications can develop.
고혈당.e: Literally 'high blood sugar', a word-for-word match with English.
고혈당.t: Pronounced [고혈땅]: ㄷ after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words becomes tense.
